title: Cross-functional roadmap quick-capture (Product / Eng / Applied ML) - prep + followups
content:
Context / why I made this: quick scratchpad for tomorrow’s 45m cross-functional sync (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Goal is to leave with crisp next-step decisions for the Hosted API routing and caching experiments, and a clear owner map for the new model-variant fallback plan. This is intentionally rough — use during the meeting, then convert to a proper follow-up doc if we get traction.

Meeting details:
- When: 2026-03-13 10:00–10:45 PT
- Who I expect: Pri (product), Marco (serving runtime), Riley (applied ML), Sofia (product PM for hosted API), Jaya (infra), me (eng product), optional: Theo (observability)
- Outcome we need: 1) decide experiment priority & sizing for prefix cache improvement vs KV-cache sharing; 2) agree on canary rollout policy for model-variant fallbacks; 3) assign owners + 2wk checkpoints.

Quick background (2–3 lines we can say out loud):
- Product has several customer-wide issues: customer A saw doubled cost on text-gen bursts; Product wants a short-term mitigant and medium-term architecture changes.
- Eng (runtime) has two proposals: A) Optimize prefix-level cache + automatic TTL tuning (low infra change), B) KV-cache sharing across warm-up sessions with model-variant compatibility mapping (higher risk/infra work).
- Applied ML has a fast-approx model variant (quantized q2) that loses ~1.5 ROUGE on a small eval but saves ~45% perf. Need to decide acceptable rollback thresholds.

Agenda (compact; timeboxed):
1) 5m quick context + data snapshot (me)
2) 10m Eng presents perf/cost estimates for Prefix-TTL vs KV-share (Marco)
3) 8m Applied ML presents quality deltas + uncertainty bounds for q2 variant (Riley)
4) 10m Discuss canary & rollback policy (Pri + Sofia)
5) 7m Decide experiment priority + owner assignments
6) 5m Quick meeting notes capture / next steps (me)

Data snapshot I’ll show (slides -> paste into chat):
- Recent 14-day token breakdown: 62% short generation (<64 tokens), 28% 64–512, 10% >512 (source: analytics route-level daily sample)
- Cost delta observed from customer A burst window: +210% token cost (mostly many repeated prefixes)
- Current cache hit rate (prefix-based): 18%; estimated headroom to 40% with tuned TTL for recurring prefixes
- KV cache warm-up 95% hit after 30s for steady traffic (but cold start still expensive)

Key trade-offs to highlight (one-liners):
- Prefix-TTL tuning = fast to ship, limited infra risk, incremental gains for short gen workloads; does not address cold-start or variant-level reuse.
- KV-share across sessions = higher throughput upside for extended sessions and model variants, but requires consistency checks and slightly more memory pressure.
- q2 quantized variant = large perf wins, small measured quality drop; risk: unknown regressions on edge prompt families (long-form summarization).

Decision prompts (phrased as yes/no to accelerate):
- Do we prioritize Prefix-TTL experiment immediately (2-week sprint) or invest infra resources into KV-share first?
- For canarying q2 variant, do we allow 2% production traffic baseline with auto-fallback if eval regressions exceed 2 ROUGE (or equivalent metric)?
- Do we require a small canned prompt suite (20 prompts) representing long-form summarize + multi-turn chat as a gating check before canary?

Suggested default proposals (I’m leaning to A+B parallel but staged):
- Short-term (this sprint): Kick Prefix-TTL tuning as a 1-sprint experiment (owner: Marco). Goal: 6% absolute cache hit increase on short-gen routes, measure cost savings for customer A style bursts.
- Medium-term (2–4 sprint runway): Begin design for KV-share across warm up sessions (owner: Jaya + Marco). Deliver a prototype with memory/consistency guardrails.
- Model variant rollout: Start a 2% canary for q2 variant behind a feature flag, gated by 20-prompt suite + daily quality regression alert. Owner: Riley (applied ML) + Pri (product). Auto-fallback policy: immediate rollback if daily aggregated quality drop > 2 ROUGE or latency regressions > 25th percentile baseline.

Risks / unknowns I want to surface quickly: (we should call these out so Product doesn’t promise timeline without eng sign-off)
- Prefix tuning can interact with per-customer privacy TTL policies (some customers require zero caching of prefixes). Need to enumerate customers with strict no-cache.
- Memory blowouts if KV-share is naively enabled across many models — need quota/eviction strategy.
- The q2 variant evaluation so far is on internal corpora; external customers might have different failure modes (edge prompts).

Pre-reads I want attendees to skim before meeting: (I’ll paste in chat)
- small experiment doc: CONFLUENCE /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=48239 (short)
- current analytics snapshot: S3 report (I’ll attach)
- PR with TTL heuristic: gh:serve-runtime/pull/2142

In-meeting notes template (I’ll capture):
- Decision made: <short sentence>
- Owners: <list>
- Success metrics: <numbers>
- Blockers: <list>
- Next checkpoint date: <YYYY-MM-DD>

My preferred phrasing for the canary guardrails (copy-paste friendly):
"Start q2 variant at 2% of traffic behind feature flag. Require passing 20-prompt regression suite (long-form summarize + multi-turn). Enable daily regression alerts comparing production q2 to baseline; auto-fallback if quality drop > 2 ROUGE or relative latency > 25% increase. Re-evaluate at 14 days."

Follow-ups / action items I want to leave with (pre-filled so we can assign):
- Marco: scope Prefix-TTL tuning experiment, list code diffs + perf targets, plan to ship a toggle in 1 sprint. Due: 2026-03-27
- Jaya + Marco: design doc outline for KV-share across sessions (include eviction, per-model quotas, and safety checks). Due: 2026-04-03
- Riley: assemble 20-prompt regression suite, include at least 5 long-form summarize and 5 multi-turn chat prompts; provide evaluation script. Due: 2026-03-24
- Pri / Sofia: update customer-communication template for cost-mitigation messaging (in case we need to notify customer A). Due: 2026-03-20
- Theo: add observability checks to track q2 traffic path + daily deltas (latency + ROUGE). Due: 2026-03-25
- Me (Amelia): convert meeting notes to tidy follow-up doc and post to CONFLUENCE; make follow-up Jira tasks from decisions. Due: 2026-03-14

Open questions to ask in meeting (my internal list, mark which we want answered live):
- Are there legal/contractual customers explicitly prohibiting prefix caching? (ask live)
- What is infra capacity to host KV-share prototype in dev cluster? (ask Marco/Jaya)
- Is 2 ROUGE the right threshold, or do we map to a percent drop on customer-specific metrics? (ask Product + Riley)

Notes I plan to capture in the meeting (sample quick bullets):
- If we pick Prefix-TTL only: quick win, communicate to customer within a week.
- If we pick KV-share first: higher upside but 4–6 week runway; need trade desk/infra commitment.
- Agreed to start q2 at 2% with 14-day checkpoint (if decision made).

Post-meeting checklist (what I’ll do right after):
- Snapshot the 10:00 analytics sample (for the record)
- Create Jira tasks aligned to owners above (link in Confluence follow-up)
- Ping customer success about possible comms to customer A (cc: Pri)
- Move items that need deeper discussion to a follow-up 30m technical sync (if any)

Rough personal talking points (so I don’t ramble):
- Keep it focused: we need an experimental signal this sprint vs speculative architecture.
- Ask for concrete deliverables and dates; avoid vague "we’ll evaluate" phrasing.
- Emphasize safety-first for q2 canary: users expect consistent quality.

Random scratch area (notes-to-self, unstructured):
- If Marco says KV-share needs LRU eviction, ask for exact memory delta per 1k concurrent sessions.
- Check previous internal incident: INCIDENT-2025-11 (warm-up outage) — might be relevant for risk discussion.
- Consider quick A/B against current model with prefix TTL toggled per-route instead of global (could reduce customer-level legal issues).

End scratchpad. Will tidy after meeting and push into the shared drive folder if we have concrete decisions.

-- Amelia
